meta.title: Threat Owls: security for a world run by AI agents
meta.description: Threat Owls shows you where you’re exposed, ranks what to fix first, and keeps your AI agents inside the lines.

acceptedAnswer.text: We are working with a few design partners first. Write to us and we will tell you exactly where things stand.

An AI assistant that does more than answer questions. It takes actions: reading email, opening files, calling other software, even working with other AIs. The more it can do, the more there is to protect.

mainEntity.name: Do we need a security team to use it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Reports and alerts are written in plain language, and every action is explained. If you do have a security team, it plugs into the tools they already use.

mainEntity.name: Will it slow down or break our AI tools?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start by only watching, so nothing changes. Blocking is switched on later, only for the risky actions you choose, and any action can be undone.

mainEntity.name: Does it replace our existing security tools?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It works alongside them, adds the missing view of AI agents, and shares what it finds with the systems you already run.

mainEntity.name: Will you read our private conversations?

acceptedAnswer.text: By default we record who did what, not the content. Capturing the content of prompts is optional, limited and under your control.

mainEntity.name: Can AI make the final security decisions?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AI helps explain and suggest. Allowing or blocking is done by clear rules you approve, so results are predictable and can be reviewed.

mainEntity.name: How do you rank what to fix?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every finding gets one of four verdicts: Fix now (evidence supports urgent action), Review (material, but needs a human look), Deprioritize (lower risk, with the reasons kept) or Not enough data (we say so instead of guessing). A quiet sensor means unknown, not safe.

hear.p: Think of us as a security guard for your AI workers. Businesses now let AI assistants answer customers, read email, pull reports and update records. They are fast and useful, but they can be tricked, and most security tools were never built to watch them.

sheet.h2: The map draws itself while we scan
sheet.p: We pull what your scanners, cloud, accounts and AI tools report into one map, then rank problems by what an attacker could really reach. Keep scrolling and the map completes.
sheet.aria: An exposure map building over one scan, from the network to the agents.
sheet.posterAlt: The finished exposure map of one scan.
sheet.capText: A short list of what to fix first, with the reason in plain English. This is our CTEM product.

pens.p: Every page below is drawn from the same scan. One view paints exposure, another writes the timeline of agent actions, a third rings out the blast radius of one stolen login. Like checking every door and window, then telling you which ones are actually unlocked.

out.h2: Your defenses were built for people. Agents are different.
out.p: Agents do not get phished. They obey. They carry logins, read email and files, treat hidden instructions as orders, and never slow down.

formats.title: The poisoned email
formats.desc: A support agent reads a message with hidden text telling it to send out your client list. It obeys, because it cannot tell an instruction from a message.

formats.title: The over-powered assistant
formats.desc: An agent was given admin access “just to get it working.” Trick it once and the attacker has admin access too.

formats.title: The runaway loop
formats.desc: An agent gets stuck and repeats an action thousands of times, sending email or changing records, before a person notices.

formats.title: The tool nobody approved
formats.desc: An employee connects a new AI tool to company data. IT never hears about it, so nobody is watching what it can reach.

steps.title: Discover
steps.text: We list everything you run: devices, cloud, accounts, and every AI tool and agent, plus what each one can reach.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.text: Instead of thousands of alerts, you get a short list of what to fix first, and why.

steps.title: Protect
steps.text: Rules you approve keep AI inside its limits. Risky actions wait for a person. Decoys catch anything suspicious.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Every action is recorded and explained, so you can show leaders, customers and auditors exactly what happened.

alts: Discover: every device, account, cloud service and AI agent on one map, with what each can reach.
Prioritize: thousands of findings ranked into a short list of what to fix first.
Protect: agent actions pass rules you approve; risky ones wait for a person, decoys catch the rest.
Prove: every action recorded, explained and chained, with a monthly report.

listen.h2: We watch your AI while it works
listen.p: Each AI agent gets an identity and clear limits. We check what it tries to do, and risky actions wait for a person. Harmless decoy tools that no honest agent would touch act as tripwires: if one is touched, we know something is wrong. This is our AI Defender product.
listen.fine: Like a guard who knows who belongs in each room, plus a tripwire in the vault corridor.
listen.alt: AI Defender live activity: every agent action, what was allowed, blocked or held for approval.

privacy.h2: AI helps you think. Rules decide.
privacy.p: A product that guards AI cannot itself be an unpredictable AI. AI explains findings, spots gaps and drafts policies, always showing its sources. Allow, deny and approval come from tested policy that you can read, replay and roll back.

price.h2: Two products, one picture of risk
price.p: CTEM finds and ranks what is exposed. AI Defender keeps your agents inside the lines. They share one map: what an agent can reach decides what it may do, and what it actually does flows back into the map.

scan.h2: Scan your site in twenty seconds
scan.p: A free outside-in check: the same first look an attacker, or an AI agent, takes at your domain. Email spoofing, HTTPS, security headers, DNS, and the rules you set for AI crawlers, each answered as Fix now, Review or Looks good, with why it matters and what to do.
scan.label: Your website address
scan.note: Passive checks only: public DNS records and a few ordinary page requests. Nothing is attacked or stored.
scan.badHost: That does not look like a website address. Try something like yourcompany.com.
scan.failed: The scan could not finish. Check your connection and try again.
idleSteps: Email: who may send as you (SPF)
DNS: signed records and certificate rules
AI: rules for AI crawlers and agents
scan.fixN: You have {n} things to fix now
scan.reviewN: Nothing urgent. {n} things worth a review.
scan.clean: Nothing to fix from the outside.
